claims.text: We introduce a clinician-in-the-loop framework featuring a clinically and technically-informed error taxonomy to classify LLM outputs.
We introduce an experimental structure to comprehensively and iteratively compare outputs within an LLM document generation pipeline.
We introduce a clinical safety framework to assess potential harms of errors in LLM outputs.
We introduce CREOLA, a graphical user interface (GUI) designed to perform and assess clinical error taxonomy classification, output comparison, and clinical safety assessment.
The evaluation of LLMs for clinical note generation observed an overall hallucination rate of 1.47%.
Among the observed hallucinations in clinical note generation, 44% were rated as major.
The evaluation of LLMs for clinical note generation observed an overall omission rate of 3.45%.
Among the observed omissions in clinical note generation, 17% were rated as major.
Iterative prompts and workflow refinements reduced major errors below previously reported human note-taking error rates.

evidence.description: Overall, we observed a 1.47% hallucination rate across 18 experimental configurations.
Out of the 1.47% hallucination rate, 44% were rated 'major'.
Overall, we observed a 3.45% omission rate across 18 experimental configurations.
Out of the 3.45% omission rate, 17% were rated 'major'.
Through iterative prompts and workflow refinements, we reduced major errors below previously reported human note-taking error rates.

methodologies.name: Clinician-in-the-loop CREOLA framework
methodologies.description: A framework combining an error taxonomy, an iterative comparison experimental structure, a clinical safety harm assessment, and a GUI (CREOLA) to assess clinical safety and hallucination rates in LLM-generated clinical notes.
conditions: 18 experimental configurations involving LLMs for clinical note generation
